description: The best excerpt is a five-word closing line (below the old 6-word minimum); the sentence before it makes a good two-unit range, while the middle sentences lean on what came before.
sourceText: I leave Sisyphus at the foot of the mountain. One always finds one's burden again. But Sisyphus teaches the higher fidelity that negates the gods and raises rocks. He too concludes that all is well. This universe henceforth without a master seems to him neither sterile nor futile. The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
